summary: AI observability tools give teams visibility into how their LLM applications behave in production by tracing requests, evaluating output quality, and tracking token usage and spend. As LLM applications scale, uncontrolled API costs and silent quality regressions become major risks, making observability essential for reliability, debugging, and budget control. The right tool depends on your model providers, workflow complexity, and whether you prioritize evaluation, cost tracking, or full-stack monitoring.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces of LLM and agent chains, latency, token usage, costs, and evaluation/quality metrics.
features: Deep tracing for LangChain and non-LangChain apps
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39 per seat/month with overage ~$2.50 per additional traces; higher-volume Plus plans around $264 per 100,000 traces; Enterprise custom. Base data retention ~14 days.
tools.best_for: Teams building complex agentic or chained LLM workflows (especially within the LangChain ecosystem) that need rich tracing plus evaluation.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: API request/response logs, token usage, cost per request/model, latency, and caching efficiency via a lightweight proxy.
features: Strong per-model cost tracking and analytics
tools.pricing: Free tier available; usage-based paid plans around $79 per 100,000 traces; 30-day data retention on paid tiers; Enterprise custom.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting fast setup and strong, affordable cost tracking—especially when OpenAI or a single provider is the primary model source.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt/response quality, model experiments, evaluations, and end-to-end ML/LLM lifecycle metrics (via W&B Weave).
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
Strong integration with the broader ML training ecosystem
tools.pricing: Free personal/academic tier; team and enterprise plans are usage- and seat-based (custom pricing for scaled usage).
tools.best_for: ML and research teams that want LLM observability alongside full model experiment tracking and the broader MLOps lifecycle.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production model and LLM performance, drift, embeddings, hallucination/quality metrics, traces, and token/cost usage.
features: LLM tracing and evaluation (including open-source Arize Phoenix)
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is free and open-source; Arize AX offers a free tier with paid Pro and Enterprise plans at custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing production-grade monitoring, drift detection, and deep evaluation—plus a free open-source option (Phoenix) for local tracing.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, nested spans, token usage and costs, latency, prompt versions, and evaluation scores.
features: Detailed nested tracing for agents and chains
tools.pricing: Free open-source self-hosted tier; cloud Hobby (free), Core/Pro, and Enterprise plans with usage-based pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting a flexible, open-source, framework-agnostic observability stack with strong tracing and prompt management.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, traces, token usage, latency, and costs using OpenTelemetry-standard instrumentation.
features: Built on the OpenTelemetry open standard
Vendor-neutral—export to Datadog, Grafana, Honeycomb, etc.
tools.pricing: Free and open-source; costs come only from your chosen OpenTelemetry backend or Traceloop's managed offering (custom pricing).
tools.best_for: Engineering teams that already use OpenTelemetry/standard observability tooling and want vendor-neutral, standards-based LLM instrumentation.

cost_tips: Enable response caching for repeated or similar prompts (tools like Helicone make this easy) to avoid paying for identical completions multiple times.
Route requests to the cheapest capable model—use smaller/faster models for simple tasks and reserve premium models (e.g., GPT-4-class) only when needed.
Trim prompt and context size: shorten system prompts, limit RAG context chunks, and set sensible max_token limits to reduce both input and output token costs.
Monitor token usage and set per-user or per-feature budgets and alerts so you catch runaway costs and inefficient prompts early before they compound.
